content.comment_body: I have several [product_name] basic modules [version_no] and an expansion module [version_no] that have never been used. Now I want to set up and use them. However, this reserve basic module [version_no] continuously displays an hourglass and keeps restarting. Because of this, I purchased a new basic module [version_no] (with the newest firmware [version_no]) and added it to my network. In [product_name] [version_no] (updated from [version_no]) I see all my modules and can go online. Still, I'm unable to connect or transfer my program to the new basic module [version_no]. I’ve tried everything I could imagine. My IP (only the last part is different), subnet settings (unchanged) are correct, and I’ve disabled the firewall and antivirus. I’ve tried both Windows 10 and Windows 11. I've also isolated the module from others, connected directly to the PC, and placed it in the network, but nothing works. Does anyone know what could be wrong?

This issue can have various causes, but it usually relates to your network setup. For example, the module might be inside your router’s DHCP range and the address could be conflicting or duplicated. Have you tried letting [product_name] search for the module?

This doesn't seem to be an IP issue. There must be another cause. Is there any licensing restriction that prevents connecting with the new basic module [version_no] when using the updated [product_name] [version_no]?

If your original [product_name] version [version_no] was a full licensed version (not a demo), then the software upgrade should be properly licensed. To connect your PC to a current basic module [version_no] through [product_name], you need [product_name] [version_no].
